reasoning_summary: The convection scheme is first-order Gauss upwind. It adds numerical diffusion that damps the wake and shear layers. That directly biases the mean drag and the shedding frequency, and nothing in the evidence bounds the bias at 3 %.

The mesh is coarse for resolving the wake. It has 30580 cells, a representative cell size of 0.45745 D, and a last wake cell of 1.0209 D. Together with first-order upwind, this makes strong discretisation error likely. The evidence has no mesh or scheme refinement to show the results are converged.

The reported Strouhal frequency resolution is 0.013333. Against St = 0.12614 that is about 10 % of the value. The FFT and zero-crossing estimates (0.12605 and 0.12581) agree closely, but the frequency-resolution limit is still much coarser than the 3 % target.

Statistical stationarity is only marginal. The stationary window start is the MSER cap (67.226), and the drag drift is 0.010692 relative. That is about a third of the 3 % budget before any discretisation error. The 95 % confidence interval on mean drag is small (0.0034414), so sampling noise is not the main problem.

Setup items are acceptable: blockage ratio 0.0125, uniform inlet at 0.15, reference quantities consistent with D = 0.01 and U = 0.15, Courant number 0.73198, checkMesh ok, 10 stationary cycles, and mass imbalance 0.0. These do not offset the first-order scheme on a coarse mesh with no verification evidence, so the quantities cannot be trusted to 3 %.
